I love this game, it is very fun and engaging and has a simplistic but visually good art style, however whenever the devs decide to add something it breaks many other things. Especially for people on mixed reality headsets, who have all reported and complained about stuttering and random crashes for awhile now with no good response or fix. I myself have experienced it, and it makes the game unplayable and ruins it.

EDIT: Changing this review to a positive one! Upon recently playing it once again with my friend I pleasantly found that my stuttering was DRASTICALLY reduced to sparse minor flickers here and there. Instead of the entire application freezing up and throwing me into the SteamVR space after something happened. Many slight and positive changes have also been added along with the fixes this which address all of the complaints i'd made earlier and improves on features like customization, ui, etc. The game is now playable to WMR again!

I've played Rec Room since early this year, first starting to play on my Oculus Quest 2. It's quite a fun experience, with a lot of friendly people and a whole bunch of variety with the games that you can play. If I were to describe it simply, it's like VRChat but with people who won't treat you like garbage over the smallest things.

It's hard to put into words how much Rec Room meant to so many of us what started as just a game became a place where friendships were made memories were created and countless hours of laughter were shared for many people it wasnt just somewhere to play it was somewhere to belong.

The removal of Rec Room feels like losing a small part of our daily lives the rooms we explored the events we joined the late night conversations and the people we met along the way all became a part of our story while games come and go, the experiences and connections we built there will always stay with us.

Thank you Rec Room, for the memories the adventures and the community you brought together even if the game is gone the moments we shared within it will never be forgotten.
